doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Rehearsals with his group
summary: Rehearsals are long debates; they repeat tunes until he says they are right, because audiences know these songs.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: You have rehearsals. Let’s see. Who was I . . .? I talked to . . .
Oh you mean of the group?
They’re like a series of argumentation and debate. They’re fantastic. They deal with almost everything but music.
I talked to Miles Griffith recently. I didn’t get a chance to talk too much. I wanted to know, what are the rehearsals like? What do you rehearse? What do you do?
He said, “We just keep going over the same thing until Jon says it’s right,” or something like that.

Yeah. That’s true. That’s true. I like it to be right, because then people will hear it. Because people already know these tunes that we do. They’re part of America’s culture, and I think if you do them wrong, people know. They may not be musicians. They may not have any real sophistication and be able to articulate their ideas, but their ears, I think, are good, and they know what they’re hearing. So I like it to be right.
